assumptions: the stated frequency and wavelength refer to the same travelling wave on the string

defect_reasons.invalid_numerical_precision: The certified answer is displayed as 20 m/s, but v = 6.0 Hz * 3.0 m = 18 m/s; with two-significant-figure inputs, 20 m/s is rounded so far that it is wrong (an 11% error).

counterexamples: Any rendering: f * lambda = 6.0 * 3.0 = 18.0 m/s, not the certified 20 m/s.
notes: Governing equation v = f*lambda, parameters (6.0 Hz, 3.0 m), units (Hz*m = m/s) and the invariance argument (cable age has no path to the target) are all correct and agree with pass 1. The only defect is the certified answer display of 20 m/s; the correct value at the stated precision is 18 m/s. Whether this arose from one-significant-figure rounding or an arithmetic slip, the displayed certified answer is wrong, so the item cannot be admitted as certified.
